correctness.rationale: The hyperbolic tile is a compact simple geodesic polygon. Klein-model triangulation reduces diameter to original vertex pairs by convexity of distance along each geodesic. At the explicit lower and upper vertices, the maximum cosh distances are 1+(q+1)^2/(2q^4), 1+1/(2q^2), and 1+(2q^2+2q+1)/(2q^3(q+1)). Cross minus lower has numerator q^3-q^2-2q-1, negative only at integer q=2; all extremal pairs follow. The arcosh small-argument limit and exact source area imply both sqrt(2) asymptotics.

It supplies sharp asymptotic constant sqrt(2), identifies all farthest pairs, and reveals the q=2 branch transition. A future comparison of efficient small hyperbolic tiles can use this precise benchmark, independent of any general minimization theorem.
